props.gloss_en: one who traps a bird into a tower is liable (stated by R' Yehuda, and by the Sages)
R' Yehuda: one who traps a deer into a house is liable
the Sages: one who traps a deer into a garden, a courtyard or enclosures is liable
the Beitza mishna: one may not trap fish from enclosures on Yom Tov, nor put food before them
the Beitza mishna: but one may trap a beast [from enclosures on Yom Tov], and put food before them
the Beitza mishna: and one may trap a bird [from enclosures on Yom Tov], and put food before them
the baraita: from enclosures of beasts one may not trap on Yom Tov, nor put food before them
the baraita: from enclosures of birds one may not trap on Yom Tov, nor put food before them
the baraita: from enclosures of fish one may not trap on Yom Tov, nor put food before them
this [the baraita, forbidding the beast] is R' Yehuda
that [the Beitza mishna, permitting the beast] is the Rabbis
this [the Beitza mishna, permitting the bird] is a roofed enclosure
that [the baraita, forbidding the bird] is an unroofed enclosure
for both R' Yehuda and the Rabbis: [trapping] a bird into a tower, yes [liable]; into a house -- which is roofed -- no
Rabba bar Rav Huna: here [a bird into a house, not trapped] we deal with a צפור דרור
Rabba bar Rav Huna: because it does not accept authority
the school of R' Yishmael: why is it called צפור דרור? because it dwells in a house as in a field
this [the baraita, forbidding the beast] is in a large enclosure
that [the Beitza mishna, permitting the beast] is in a small enclosure
what are the circumstances of a large enclosure, and of a small one?
Rav Ashi: wherever one runs after it and reaches it in one lunge -- a small enclosure; any other -- a large one
Rav Ashi, alternatively: wherever the walls' shadows fall upon each other -- a small enclosure; any other -- a large one
Rav Ashi, or alternatively: wherever there are no corners upon corners -- a small enclosure; any other -- a large one
